findings.title: Lithuanian translations replaced with Italian text
findings.body: totpStep1 in the Lithuanian account messages file was changed to "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:", which is Italian, not Lithuanian (the old text was Lithuanian). The same happens in themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties line 71 (loginTotpStep1). Lithuanian users will now see an Italian sentence on the OTP setup page.

findings.title: Traditional Chinese text inserted into Simplified Chinese file
findings.body: The new totpStep1 value "在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：" uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機/應用程式) and Traditional-style phrasing, while the rest of messages_zh_CN.properties is Simplified Chinese (手机/应用). The replacement should be "在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：".

findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size switched from i18next to Java MessageFormat syntax in JS themes
findings.body: The value was changed from "Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s)." to "Attribute {0} ... {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.". The admin-ui (keycloak.v2) and account-ui (keycloak.v3) React apps render their messages via i18next, which uses {{param}} interpolation and has no support for Java MessageFormat choice patterns. With the new value, users of these JS themes will see literal "Attribute {0}" and the raw "{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}" string instead of an interpolated message. The same change was made in js/apps/account-ui/maven-resources/theme/keycloak.v3/account/messages/messages_en.properties (line 188) and js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources-community/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_zh_CN.properties. The choice-format version is only correct for the server-side Java themes under themes/src/main/resources.

findings.title: Missing English bundle crashes the verifier with a raw RuntimeException
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file path by string-replacing the absolute file path (replaceAll("resources-community", "resources") plus a locale-suffix regex) and then throws a bare RuntimeException if that file cannot be opened. Any message file whose _en counterpart is not at the exact derived location (e.g. a theme that only exists in resources-community, a differently named directory, or a file without a locale suffix such as messages.properties mapping onto itself) will abort the whole mojo with a stack trace instead of being reported as a verification message like every other problem the verifier finds. The failure should be recorded in the returned messages list (or wrapped in MojoExecutionException), and the path derivation is too fragile to be a hard precondition.

findings.title: ANCHOR_PATTERN also matches non-anchor tags starting with 'a'
findings.body: The pattern "</?a[^>]*>" used to detect anchors matches any tag whose name starts with the letter 'a' — <article>, <abbr>, <address>, <audio>, etc. — because [^>]* consumes the rest of the tag name. If a translation legitimately contains such a tag (or one is introduced later), santizeAnchors will treat it as an anchor, fail to find it in the English source, and emit a spurious "Didn't find anchor tag" error. The pattern should be "</?a(\s[^>]*)?>" so only the anchor element is matched.

findings.title: Policy allows br/p/strong/b whenever English has any HTML, including only anchors
findings.body:
The per-key policy decision is containsHtml(englishValue) ? POLICY_SOME_HTML : POLICY_NO_HTML, where containsHtml matches any tag. So for a key whose English value contains only an tag (anchors are removed afterwards by santizeAnchors), a translation may freely add ,

, or
elements that the English source never had. This is weaker than the stated intent ("only if the English source string contains HTML we also allow HTML in the translation") and lets translations introduce formatting/markup the source string does not contain.

findings.title: No test that valid translations produce no findings
findings.body: All new tests assert that violations are detected; there is no test asserting that a legitimate translation (e.g. one containing the same anchors as the English source, allowed tags like <strong>, escaped entities, or the {2,choice,...} pattern) passes with an empty message list. The verification logic relies on subtle round-trips (unescapeHtml4 on both sides, "<!-- -->" removal, anchor stripping) where a false-positive regression would only surface as build failures on the real theme files rather than a clear unit test failure.
